title: Energy from fuels; entropy and spontaneity
summary: Combustion of fuels releases energy but also pollutants and CO₂. Compare fossil fuels, biofuels and fuel cells; at HL, use entropy and Gibbs energy to predict whether reactions are spontaneous.

keyterms.definition: Burning in excess oxygen; hydrocarbons form CO₂ and H₂O only.
Burning in limited oxygen, producing CO and/or carbon (soot) as well as water.
Coal, crude oil or natural gas formed over millions of years from ancient organisms; non-renewable.
A fuel produced from recently living biomass, e.g. bioethanol from fermentation of sugars.
Energy released per unit mass of fuel (kJ kg⁻¹); energy density is per unit volume.
An electrochemical cell that converts the chemical energy of a continuously supplied fuel and oxidant directly into electrical energy.
A gas such as CO₂, CH₄ or H₂O that absorbs infrared radiation emitted by Earth, warming the atmosphere.
Describes a fuel whose combustion releases no more CO₂ than was absorbed in producing it (ideal for biofuels).
A measure of the dispersal of energy and matter (disorder) in a system; units J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS; a reaction is spontaneous when ΔG is negative.
A reaction that can occur without continuous external energy input once started; ΔG < 0. It may still be slow.
ΔG⦵ = −RT ln K: negative ΔG⦵ means K > 1, so products are favoured at equilibrium.

questions.prompt: What are the products of the complete combustion of propane?
questions.explanation: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O.
O on the right = 4 + 3 = 7; ethanol supplies 1, so O₂ provides 6 atoms → 3 O₂.

questions.statement: Carbon monoxide from incomplete combustion is toxic because it binds to haemoglobin.
questions.explanation: CO binds strongly to haemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport in the blood.

questions.prompt: Which fuel has the highest specific energy?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen releases about 141 MJ kg⁻¹, far more per mass than the others, though its energy density as a gas is low.

questions.prompt: Match each fuel to a key issue.

pairs.right: Highest CO₂ and SO₂ per unit energy
Methane leaks are a potent greenhouse gas
Competes with food crops for land
Low energy density; hard to store

questions.explanation: Choosing fuels involves trade-offs between energy, cost and environment.

questions.statement: Biofuels are exactly carbon neutral in practice.
questions.explanation: Farming, processing and transport usually involve fossil-fuel use, so net emissions are above zero.

questions.prompt: Which gas is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: N₂ is non-polar and symmetric with no IR-active vibration; it does not absorb IR.

questions.text: Bioethanol is made by ___ of sugars by yeast.
questions.explanation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (anaerobic, yeast enzymes).

questions.prompt: Order the stages by which CO₂ from fossil fuels causes warming.
items: CO₂ concentration in the atmosphere rises
CO₂ absorbs and re-emits some IR
questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing IR, not incoming visible light.

questions.prompt: In a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell, what is the only product?
questions.explanation: Overall reaction: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, producing electricity directly.

questions.prompt: Which change has the largest increase in entropy?
questions.explanation: Gases have much higher entropy than liquids; liquid → gas greatly increases dispersal.

questions.statement: A reaction with ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0 is spontaneous at all temperatures.
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS is negative for every T when ΔH is negative and ΔS positive.
T is the absolute temperature in K; watch units (ΔS in J, ΔH in kJ).

questions.prompt: ΔH = +180 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = +0.200 kJ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Above what temperature is the reaction spontaneous?
questions.explanation: ΔG = 0 when T = ΔH/ΔS = 180/0.200 = 900 K; above this TΔS exceeds ΔH.
The TΔS term grows in importance as temperature rises.

questions.statement: A spontaneous reaction always happens quickly.
questions.explanation: ΔG says nothing about rate; diamond → graphite is spontaneous but extremely slow (high Ea).

questions.prompt: If ΔG⦵ for a reaction is large and negative, the equilibrium constant K is…
questions.explanation: ΔG⦵ = −RT ln K: negative ΔG⦵ means ln K > 0, so K > 1.

questions.text: ΔS⦵ for a reaction = ΣS⦵(products) − ΣS⦵(___).
questions.explanation: Unlike ΔHf, standard entropies of elements are not zero.

questions.prompt: Order by standard entropy, lowest first.
questions.explanation: Solids < liquids < gases; more complex gas molecules have higher entropy.

questions.prompt: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g), the sign of ΔS is…
questions.explanation: 4 mol gas → 2 mol gas: fewer ways to disperse energy, so ΔS < 0.
